questions.question: A circle has radius √2 cm. It is divided into two segments by a chord of length 2 cm. Prove that the angle subtended by the chord at a point in the major segment is 45°.
solutionSteps: In triangle OAB, OA = OB = √2. Chord AB = 2.

questions.question: Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of any two chords of a circle, which are not parallel, intersect at the centre of the circle.
solutionSteps: Perpendicular bisector of chord AB contains all points equidistant from A and B.
Center O is equidistant from all points on circle, so OA = OB. Thus O lies on this bisector.
Similarly, O must lie on the perpendicular bisector of another chord CD.
The unique point of intersection of these two lines must be the centre O.

questions.question: Bisectors of angles A, B, and C of a triangle ABC intersect its circumcircle at D, E, and F respectively. Prove that the angles of triangle DEF are (90° - A/2), (90° - B/2), and (90° - C/2).
In triangle ABC, if the angle bisector of Angle A and the perpendicular bisector of side BC intersect, prove that they intersect on the circumcircle of the triangle.
solutionSteps: Let bisector of Angle A meet circumcircle at P. Then arc BP = arc PC.
This implies chord BP = chord PC.
Since P is equidistant from endpoints B and C, it must lie on the perpendicular bisector of BC.
Thus they intersect at P on the circumcircle.

questions.question: Two congruent circles intersect at points A and B. Through A, a line segment PAQ is drawn such that P and Q lie on the two circles. Prove that BP = BQ.
solutionSteps: Common chord AB in congruent circles implies arc AB (circle 1) = arc AB (circle 2).
Angles in segments by equal arcs in congruent circles are equal.
Angle APB = Angle AQB. In triangle PBQ, since base angles are equal, BP = BQ.
